Greece Files Protest With Kyiv Over Armed Ukrainian Sea Drone Found Near Lefkada — Athens on Wednesday submitted an official diplomatic protest to Kyiv over a naval drone found off the Greek island of Lefkada in May. Greek authorities said the explosive-laden vessel posed risks to civilian traffic and the environment, while claiming an investigation concluded the drone belonged to Ukraine and was part of a planned operation targeting Russian-linked vessels.

‘Nothing Stops Ukrainian Art’ – Met Opera Chief Peter Gelb — Peter Gelb, general manager of New York’s Metropolitan Opera, told Kyiv Post about the institution’s support for Ukraine since Russia’s full-scale invasion. He reflected on Ukraine’s resilience, the role of culture in wartime, and the new opera “Mothers of Kherson,” which depicts the abduction of Ukrainian children by Russia. Gelb said art can preserve memory and bear witness long after headlines fade.

Ukraine to Deliver Record 1,500 Motorcycles to Frontline Troops in 2026 — Ukraine’s Defense Procurement Agency on Wednesday signed a contract for 1,500 motorcycles for the Armed Forces, three times last year’s total motorbike buy. The contract was awarded through a competitive tender process that officials say saved nearly Hr.12 million that can now be reallocated to additional military needs.

Ukraine Is Doing Better: Notes From the Sidelines of the Black Sea Security Forum 2026 — There were many important discussions at the Black Sea Security Forum 2026 regarding security and Ukraine’s possible future strategies. However, the most important takeaway was optimism. Everyone shared the same assessment – Ukraine is in a better position than it was a year ago.

WATCH: Ukraine’s Fire Point Tests Missile for Homegrown Anti-Ballistic Shield as Air Defense Shortages Bite — Ukrainian defense company Fire Point has successfully tested its FP-7.X missile, which will serve as the basis for the planned FREYJA anti-ballistic defense system, providing Kyiv with a lower-cost alternative to Patriot interceptors amid ongoing air defense missile shortages.

Finland Seizes €3.7 Million in Russian Funds to Compensate Naftogaz — Finland’s National Enforcement Authority has frozen nearly €4 million belonging to Russia following a compensation claim by Naftogaz. The funds are part of a broader effort to enforce an international arbitration ruling that ordered Moscow to pay billions of euros for the expropriation of Ukrainian energy assets in Crimea.

Japanese Lawmaker Pushes Tokyo to Sell Critically-Needed Patriot Missiles to Ukraine — Japanese National Diet Upper House Member, Councillor Matsuzawa urged the ruling coalition to export Patriot PAC-3 missiles to Ukraine, citing Russian missile strikes. He said Japan’s eased export rules allow it, while Defense Minister Koizumi said Japan is not considering it. Ukraine’s President Zelensky plans to discuss missile shortages at a G7 meeting in France.

Europe Considers Fresh Push for Russia Talks Amid War Fatigue and Shifting Frontlines — German officials on Wednesday said a limited diplomatic “window” with Russia on Ukraine may be opening, with the E3 potentially leading talks. The US, Russia, and Ukraine remain divided, while analysts and EU officials warn Moscow may be using escalation to pressure negotiations. Kyiv says Russia is losing battlefield initiative and facing setbacks.

Deep Into Russia: Ukraine Damages Navy Ships in Kronstadt Port Near St. Petersburg — The Ukrainian military on Wednesday said they struck ships and infrastructure at the Kronstadt naval base in Russia’s Leningrad region, one of the key Baltic Fleet facilities near St. Petersburg. Zelensky confirmed the attack while Ukrainian officials reported damage to Russian vessels, including a corvette undergoing repairs.

Zelensky Gives Officials One Week to Finalize Patriot Deal, Or Face Personnel ‘Conclusions’ — Zelensky said Ukraine already has a political-level agreement to purchase additional Patriot air defense systems, but implementation has stalled at the legal, financial and technical stages. The president instructed officials to accelerate the process and warned that failure to deliver results could trigger personnel changes.

Day 1556 – Biletsky and Rubio, Russia Blows Up Stuff to be Scary, Smoke on the M-14 — Ukraine is intensifying a sustained drone campaign targeting Russian logistics, particularly along key southern supply routes such as the M‑14 corridor to Crimea. At the same time, battlefield assessments from commander Andriy Biletsky suggest improved conditions for Ukrainian forces, while US Secretary of State Marco Rubio signaled waning US engagement in mediation efforts.

Romania Wants to Boost Air Defence After Drone Strike Blamed on Russia — Romania’s foreign minister said the country must strengthen air defence with NATO support after a drone strike near its Ukraine border injured two people. While not confirming intent, she blamed Russia for responsibility. Bucharest is seeking short-term NATO help and joint anti-drone cooperation with Kyiv amid repeated drone incursions.

Syrsky Urges Efficient Use of Air Defense Missiles Amid Shortages, Increased Kremlin Attacks — During a visit to Air Command South, Gen. Oleksandr Syrsky reviewed Ukraine’s air defense operations and said the military must maximize the effectiveness of available systems amid ongoing shortages of air defense missiles. He also emphasized the need to expand drone interception units and integrate new technologies to counter Russia’s evolving tactics.

‘Systemic’ Retaliation: Kremlin Shrugs Off Questions After Ukraine Hits St. Petersburg Targets — The Kremlin on Wednesday said Russia’s response to Ukrainian strikes is already “systemic” after drones hit targets in the St. Petersburg area, including an oil terminal. Moscow gave no details on new retaliation plans. Ukraine said it struck multiple military-linked sites, including naval and industrial facilities deep inside Russia.

US Officials Reappear at Russia’s Top Economic Forum After Nearly a Decade — Putin aide Ushakov confirmed that a US delegation, led by Head of the US Federal Commission of Fine Arts Rodney Mims Cook, is visiting the SPIEF 2026 to talk about cultural ties amid a wider push from the West to separate culture from politics despite Russia’s ongoing invasion of Ukraine.

Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Plant Loses External Power Temporarily After Drone Strike — The IAEA said the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant lost off-site power for the 17th time since the start of the full-scale war after a drone hit a nearby substation. Backup diesel generators provided electricity until the connection was restored about 20 minutes later.

Same US Pilot Shot Down Twice Over Iran — According to CBS News on Tuesday, the same US Air Force pilot was shot down twice within weeks during the current conflict with Iran. After surviving a friendly-fire incident involving Kuwaiti air defenses, the pilot was later rescued following the downing of an F-15E over Iran. Military officials described the case as an extraordinarily rare occurrence.

Hungary Ends Two-Year Block on Ukraine Arms Payouts — Hungary has lifted its long-standing veto on EU arms reimbursements for Ukraine, unlocking €6.6 billion under the European Peace Facility after a two-year blockade. The move marks a shift in Budapest’s policy under new leadership and eases tensions within the EU over delayed military support. It also paves the way for further funding, potential accession progress for Ukraine, and a broader reset in Hungary’s relations with Brussels and Kyiv.

NATO Chief Rutte Arrives in Kyiv in Surprise Visit — NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte arrived in Kyiv on Wednesday in an unannounced visit, underscoring continued Alliance support for Ukraine. Ukrzaliznytsia briefly confirmed his arrival at Kyiv railway station before deleting the post, though images circulated online. Details of Rutte’s agenda are currently undisclosed.

Armenia Votes – Russia Piles on the Pressure — Armenians head to the polls on June 7 in a high-stakes election that could determine whether the country continues Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan’s pro-Western shift or remains tied to Russia’s orbit. Moscow has increased pressure through economic threats and political rhetoric, while supporters of European integration argue the vote has effectively become a referendum on Armenia’s geopolitical future and independence from Russian influence.

Exclusive: Anne Applebaum Says Ukraine Is Becoming a Security Provider, Not Just a Security Consumer — Speaking to Kyiv Post after interviewing Kyrylo Budanov at the Security Architecture Forum in Kyiv, Anne Applebaum said Ukraine’s military achievements, particularly in drone warfare, have altered international perceptions of the country. She argued that Ukraine is increasingly viewed as a contributor to European and global security and should use this moment to help shape the continent’s futur

Kostyuk Reaches Historic French Open Semifinal, Dedicates Win to Ukraine — Ukrainian tennis star Marta Kostyuk advanced to her first Grand Slam semifinal with a three-set victory over compatriot Elina Svitolina at the French Open. After the match, Kostyuk said representing Ukraine mattered more than winning titles as she reflected on the deadly Russian attacks that struck her country hours before she took the court.

Ukraine, Estonia Agree to Expand Defense Cooperation During Svyrydenko Visit — During a visit to Tallinn, Ukraine’s Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko met with Estonia’s president, parliament speaker and prime minister. The sides agreed to deepen defense cooperation, including in unmanned systems, discussed new sanctions against Russia and efforts to counter Moscow’s shadow fleet, and highlighted Estonia’s continued support for Ukraine’s energy sector and reconstruction projects.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, June 2, 2026 — Latest from the Institute for the Study of War.

Ukraine Targets St. Petersburg Oil Hub, Kronstadt Military Facilities as Putin’s ‘Davos’ Opens — President Zelensky confirmed that Ukrainian forces struck several strategic targets inside Russia overnight, including the St. Petersburg oil terminal, military facilities at the Kronstadt naval base, and a defense industry enterprise in the Tambov region. The attack sparked a major fire near St. Petersburg as the St. Petersburg International Economic Forum, often dubbed the “Russian Davos,” was set

US Military Says It Has ‘Defeated’ Iran Missile, Drone Attacks in Gulf — The US military said it defeated a series of Iranian missile and drone attacks in the Gulf and struck an Iranian military facility on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. US Central Command denied Iranian claims that US bases in Bahrain and the region were hit, saying all attacks failed. The incidents came despite a US-Iran ceasefire in place since April 8.

Sybiha: Russia Resorts to Terror Because It Is Losing on Battlefield — Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said Russia’s massive overnight attack showed Moscow is losing on the battlefield and has “no cards except terror.” He urged allies to fund Patriot systems, tighten sanctions, use frozen Russian assets and open EU negotiation clusters for Ukraine.

Zelensky Expected to Attend G7 Summit in France as Russian Attacks Intensify — President Volodymyr Zelensky is expected to attend the 52nd G7 Summit in France in mid-June as Ukraine seeks urgent air defense support amid intensified Russian missile and drone attacks. Kyiv is expected to push for more Patriot interceptors, stronger European anti-ballistic capabilities, energy resilience funding and continued pressure on Moscow through sanctions and frozen Russian assets.

Ukrainian Musician and Soldier Yaroslav ‘Varnak’ Ivanov Killed on Front Line at 23 — Yaroslav “Varnak” Ivanov, a 23-year-old Ukrainian musician, writer and soldier, was killed on May 31 while carrying out a combat mission. Known online as @radykalniy, he served in the military from age 19 and later joined an electronic warfare unit. Friends remembered him as honest, bright and deeply devoted to Ukraine.

UN Chief Condemns Massive Russian Missile and Drone Attack That Killed 22 in Ukraine — UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres strongly condemned Russia’s overnight missile and drone barrage on Ukraine, which killed at least 22 people and injured more than 130. President Zelensky renewed calls for Patriot interceptors and a stronger European anti-ballistic shield.

Zelensky: Foreign Components ‘Complicit in Killings’ as Russia’s Overnight Strike Kills 22, Including 2 Children, Injures 130 — President Volodymyr Zelensky has confirmed the number of casualties in Russia’s overnight assault, with 22 people killed and 130 injured, including two children. More than 70 missiles and over 650 drones were launched overnight, followed by nearly 100 more drone strikes throughout the day. He warned of every missile and drone being dependent on imported components, call

Budanov: Russia’s Top Fear Is Threats to Putin’s Regime — The Kremlin’s main concern is not Russia’s struggling economy but the erosion of Putin’s grip on power, the head of Ukraine’s Presidential Office said. He argued that growing awareness of the war inside Russia is putting pressure on Moscow, while stressing that any settlement must include security guarantees for Ukraine.

Zelensky Warns Russia Targeting Military Industry, Foreign Partners: ‘We Will Respond’ — President Volodymyr Zelensky warns Moscow is preparing new military, political, and propaganda attacks against Ukraine’s missile sector and foreign partnerships. He says Russia now treats Ukraine’s ability to develop its own ballistic systems and anti-missile defense as a strategic threat, seeking to limit Kyiv’s ties with Moldova, the South Caucasus, the Middle East and the Gulf region.

Hungary Signals Breakthrough on Ukraine, Moldova-EU Talks — Hungary is preparing to lift its long-running veto on Ukraine’s EU bid, as new leadership signals openness for Kyiv and Chisinau to launch the first cluster of accession talks at a conference in Luxembourg, June 15. The shift follows recent negotiations on the rights of ethnic Hungarians in Ukraine and comes as EU ambassadors rush to finalize a joint position. Budapest says any formal decisions are yet to be made, but the political sign

Svyrydenko Visits Estonia, Thanks Tallinn for Military Support, Backing Ukraine’s EU Path — During her first official visit to Estonia as prime minister, Yuliia Svyrydenko met with Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal, President Alar Karis and parliamentary speaker Lauri Hussar. The talks focused on defense cooperation, military assistance, sanctions against Russia and reconstruction projects, with Svyrydenko thanking Tallinn for its continued support of Ukraine.

Former President Poroshenko on Ceasefire, 2014 Lessons, Trump, and UN — In a wide-ranging discussion at the Black Sea Security Forum 2026, former Ukrainian President Petro Poroshenko reflected on Ukraine’s transformation since 2014, arguing that the country has broken decisively with its Soviet past, built Europe’s strongest army, and must pursue EU and NATO membership as the foundation of its long-term security.

EU Prepares 21st Russia Sanctions Package, Targeting Oil Revenues and Shadow Fleet — As of Tuesday, EU officials are working on the 21st sanctions package against Russia, expected to be presented next week. The proposed measures would tighten restrictions on Russian oil exports, expand sanctions on energy companies and shadow fleet vessels, and could include new penalties against Russian Orthodox Patriarch Kirill.

Russian Strike Damages Residential Quarter of Kyiv’s UNIT.City Innovation Park — Tuesday’s Russian strike on  Kyiv damaged the UNIT.Home residential complex at UNIT.City, Ukraine’s flagship innovation park, shattering windows and damaging facades. The management company said it is assessing losses and preparing a step-by-step recovery plan in coordination with residents and city authorities.

Putin Makes Criminal Record Certificate Mandatory for Russian Citizenship Applicants – Except Ukrainians — Under a new decree signed by Putin on Tuesday, foreign nationals and stateless persons applying for Russian citizenship must provide documents confirming they have no criminal convictions or disclosing any past convictions. The measure follows broader efforts by Russian lawmakers to tighten immigration and citizenship rules, while maintaining simplified pathways for Ukrainians from occupied

‘Fundamental Decision Made’: Russian Lawmaker Predicts New Mobilization This Fall — Russian State Duma deputy Gurulev said a new large-scale mobilization could be announced this fall, arguing that Russia’s winter-spring offensive failed to achieve expected results and that frontline losses remain high. Analysts from the IISS and ISW have previously warned that the Kremlin may eventually need additional mobilization measures as existing recruitment efforts struggle to sustain the war in Ukraine.

Germany’s Schröder Reportedly in Moscow — The former German chancellor – Putin’s proposed EU negotiator rebuffed by Europe itself – is said to be in Moscow on Tuesday, though the purpose of his visit remains unclear. Schröder has been accused of being a Russian lobbyist and was the key figure in making the first Nord Stream pipeline a reality.

Poland Reportedly Backs EU Plan to Restrict Protection for Some Ukrainian Men — Poland is pushing the EU to revise temporary protection rules for Ukrainian refugees, arguing that military-age men should not automatically qualify for the status. The proposal is part of wider EU discussions on extending or reforming refugee protections beyond 2027, though existing beneficiaries would remain unaffected.

NABU Uncovers $4M Corruption Scheme at Energoatom Hydropower Project — NABU and SAPO on Tuesday announced suspicions against two individuals in a corruption case involving the Tashlyk Pumped Storage Hydroelectric Power Plant. Investigators allege that equipment procurement contracts were manipulated through a controlled foreign intermediary, inflating costs by almost Hr.170 million and causing major losses to the state-owned energy company Energoatom.

Polish Far-Right Calls for Block of Ukraine’s EU Bid Over ‘Heroes of the UPA’ Unit — Polish far-right leader Krzysztof Bosak said Poland should block Ukraine’s EU membership bid in response to Kyiv’s decision to grant an elite military unit the honorary title “Heroes of the UPA.” The comments mark the latest escalation in a growing dispute over the legacy of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army, which – eight decades later – remains one of the most sensitive issues in Polish-Ukrainian relations.

Kremlin Warned: War Spending Is Breaking the Budget — Senior Russian officials have warned President Vladimir Putin that war spending in Ukraine is becoming unsustainable and risks widening the budget deficit, Bloomberg reports. Internal divisions are emerging between fiscal authorities calling for cuts and security officials pushing to maintain defence spending despite rising economic strain.

Russian Official Says Crimea Gas Crisis ‘Temporary’ as Ukrainian Drones Pound Infrastructure — Ukrainian drone strikes on fuel supply routes to occupied Crimea have disrupted deliveries, causing widespread fuel shortages, long queues, rationing, and travel delays. Russian officials call the situation temporary, but attacks on rail, storage, and ferry infrastructure continue to strain supplies.

Russia Hits Key Naftogaz Facility in Kharkiv Region in Double-Tap Strike — Russian forces on Tuesday attacked a key Naftogaz facility in the Kharkiv region with drones and missiles in a double-tap strike aimed at both infrastructure and emergency responders. The attack came during a nationwide assault involving 729 drones and missiles, one of the largest in the ongoing war.

Detained Russia-Linked Tanker Arrives in France — France detained and brought a suspected Russian “shadow fleet” tanker, Tagor, into port after boarding it at sea with British help over alleged false flag use. The ship is linked to sanctioned oil transport networks. Russia called the seizure “piracy” as tensions over sanctions enforcement escalate.

US Eyes Expanded Nuclear Weapons Deployment Across Europe — The US, as of Tuesday, is considering expanding nuclear-capable deployments to more NATO countries in Europe to reassure allies amid troop reductions and shifting US priorities. Talks remain early and sensitive. Eastern NATO states, especially Poland, show interest, while Russia’s opposition to NATO expansion and its war in Ukraine shape the backdrop.

Zelensky: Europe Needs Anti-Ballistic Shield After 73 Missiles, 656 Drones Strike — President Zelensky on Tuesday called for Europe to develop its own anti-ballistic missile defense system after Russia launched a massive overnight strike involving 656 drones and 73 missiles. He said the attack, which killed at least 17 people and injured over 100, shows that Ukraine and Europe remain vulnerable without stronger air defenses. Zelensky also stressed the need for continued US support in supplying P

Trump Called Netanyahu ‘F**king Crazy’ Over Lebanon Escalation – Axios — Trump reportedly confronted Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a heated phone call on Monday over Israel’s military operations in Lebanon, according to Axios. Trump allegedly warned that further escalation could isolate Israel internationally and jeopardize ongoing negotiations with Iran.

Drone Strike in Romania: How Should Nato Respond? — A Russian explosive drone strike on a residential building in Galați, Romania, near Ukraine’s port of Reni, has reignited debate over NATO’s response to growing security threats. Commentators argue that diplomatic measures are insufficient, urging stronger military deterrence, enhanced air defences, and a shift from viewing Eastern Europe as NATO’s flank to seeing it as the alliance’s frontline against Russian aggression.

Trump Reportedly Asks Xi to Lean on Putin as Ukraine Peace Talks Stall — Trump reportedly asked the Chinese leader to pressure Putin to return to negotiations with Ukraine after peace talks stalled. The appeal comes as Ukraine regains ground on the battlefield, Russian forces show signs of exhaustion, and Moscow intensifies large-scale drone and missile attacks.

Trump’s Ex-Adviser: Iran Crisis Shows NATO Growing More Important, not Less — NATO is becoming increasingly vital as Europe faces growing security risks from Iran, former US national security adviser John Bolton said in an interview with TVP World. He warned that Iranian activities and missile capabilities could directly threaten Europe and should not be viewed solely as a US concern. Bolton also criticized Washington’s lack of coordination with allies and said uncertainty over US strategy in th

4th Strike This Year: Ukrainian Drones Target Key Russian Refinery Amid Fuel Crunch — Ukraine targeted the Ilsky Oil Refinery in Russia’s Krasnodar region, marking the fourth reported strike on the facility this year. The attack comes as Ukrainian strikes continue to disrupt Russia’s oil sector, contributing to declining refinery output, rising fuel prices, and fuel rationing measures that have now spread from occupied Crimea to the Moscow region.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, June 1, 2026 — Latest from the Institute for the Study of War.

21 Killed, Over 100 Wounded in Massive Overnight Russian Missile and Drone Barrage Across Ukraine — Russia launched a massive combined missile and drone attack across Ukraine in the early hours of Tuesday, killing at least 21 people and injuring over 100 others. Kyiv reported 6 killed and 79 injured, including 3 children, while Dnipro reported 15 killed, including 2 children, and at least 37 wounded. Kharkiv and Kyiv region were also hit, with fires, damaged residential buildings, and power outa

Russian Attack on Dnipro Kills 12, Including 2 Kids, Kharkiv Also Hit — Russian overnight strikes killed 12 people and wounded at least 37 in Dnipro, Ukrainian authorities said. The attack partially destroyed a two-story building and damaged apartments in a four-story building. Kharkiv was also hit in two districts as Russia launched a wider missile and drone assault across Ukraine, including Kalibr cruise missiles, ballistic threats, drone groups and strikes on Kyiv.

Russia Strikes Kyiv in Overnight Missile and Drone Attack, People Feared Trapped Under Rubble — Russia struck Kyiv in a combined overnight missile and drone attack in the early hours of Tuesday, damaging residential buildings, causing fires and triggering power outages in several districts. Authorities reported possible people under rubble in Podilskyi district and fires in residential and civilian areas.

Russian Strikes on Dnipro and Kharkiv Injure Civilians, Damage Buildings — Russian forces struck Kharkiv and Dnipro in the early hours of Tuesday, injuring civilians and causing fires. Kharkiv reported hits in the Osnovianskyi and Slobidskyi districts, while in Dnipro a 73-year-old woman was hospitalized in a serious condition after a two-story building was partially destroyed. The attacks came during a wider Russian missile and drone assault that triggered alerts across much of Ukraine.

Ukraine Under Large-Scale Air Alert as Russia Attacks With Missiles and Drones — Russia launched a large-scale overnight missile and drone attack on Ukraine in the early hours of Tuesday, triggering air raid alerts in Kyiv and across multiple regions. Ukraine’s Air Force warned of ballistic threats from the east and north east, groups of drones, missile attacks on Dnipro and Zaporizhzhia, and Kalibr cruise missile launches from the Caspian Sea.

Zelensky Thanks France After Navy Intercepts Russian Shadow Fleet Tanker — President Zelensky thanked France after its navy intercepted the Russian-linked tanker Tagor and urged Europe to modernize its laws so such vessels can be seized, not just stopped. He said Russian oil money should fund protection against aggression, as Ukraine’s strikes have already hit 15 Russian refineries and knocked out nearly 40 percent of Russia’s primary refining capacity.

'Time to Tell Our Friend No': Ben-Gvir Urges Netanyahu to Defy Trump, Hit Hezbollah Despite Claimed Ceasefire — Donald Trump announced Israel and Hezbollah agreed to stop all attacks. His statement was undercut domestically by Ben-Gvir, who posted that “a strong minister” must know when to tell a US president “no,” insisting on continuation of Hezbollah strikes and “unleashing” of Israeli forces in the north.

Zelensky Wants War’s ‘Hot Phase’ Ended Before Winter, Budanov Says — President Volodymyr Zelensky has tasked Ukrainian officials with pursuing an end to the active phase of the war before winter, according to Presidential Office chief Kyrylo Budanov. He said Ukraine has the capabilities to work toward that goal, while acknowledging that Russia could still reject any agreements.

Zelensky: Ukraine Can Strike Russian Logistics Across All Occupied Territory — In his latest Telegram post, Zelensky highlighted Ukraine’s growing ability to strike Russian logistics hubs far behind the front line with precise attacks on energy infrastructure, command centers and depots, weakening Moscow’s war capabilities and reducing pressure on Ukrainian troops.

Former Polish Ambassador Returns Ukrainian Honor Over UPA Dispute — Bartosz Cichocki, Poland’s former ambassador to Ukraine, returned a Ukrainian state decoration awarded by President Volodymyr Zelensky in protest over Kyiv’s decision to honor a military unit with the title “Heroes of the UPA.” The move adds to growing criticism from Polish officials and highlights longstanding disagreements over the legacy of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army.

Putin Tasks FSB With Creating ‘White List’ Internet System — The Kremlin leader Vladimir Putin’s new directive deepens Russia’s shift from traditional blocking of “undesirable” sites to a system where only state-approved resources are reliably accessible, giving the FSB broader control over networks, reinforcing the Kremlin’s ability to quickly reshape or restrict online space.

Polish Official Says Zelensky Should Apologize Over UPA Row — Marcin Przydacz, head of Poland’s Bureau of International Policy, said Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky should apologize to Polish President Karol Nawrocki over Kyiv’s decision to name a military unit after the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA).

Why Putin Thinks He Can Still Win — Kyiv Post Special Correspondent Jason Smart looks at why Putin still thinks time is working for Moscow, why Russia’s internal weakness has not forced him to stop, and why the Kremlin’s real target is the political will behind Ukraine.

Zelensky Honors SBU Officers Behind Secret ‘Spiderweb’ Operation — President Volodymyr Zelensky presented state awards to SBU personnel for their role in Operation “Spiderweb”, a long-prepared drone strike that damaged and destroyed 41 Russian military aircraft at several airfields, saying the mission showed Ukraine can impose serious damage on Russia’s strategic aviation with precise, lower-cost systems. He framed the strike as a part of Ukraine’s broader effort to weaken Russia’s ability to pr

Merz to Gather European Leaders Ahead of NATO Summit — German Chancellor Friedrich Merz is expected to convene leaders from Germany, France, the UK, Italy and Poland later this month to prepare a common approach ahead of the July NATO summit. The meeting aims to highlight Europe’s efforts to assume greater responsibility for its own defense amid growing tensions with US President Donald Trump over NATO, military spending and the recent conflict with Iran.

Ukraine’s Refinery Campaign Forces Fuel Limits in Moscow — A growing fuel shortage in Russia has reached the Moscow region, where some gas stations have begun limiting fuel sales. Gas stations in Novaya Moskva have begun limiting gasoline sales to 60 liters (16 gallons) and diesel fuel sales to 100 liters (26 gallons) per customer. The shortages come as Ukraine continues a sustained campaign against Russian oil infrastructure, striking refineries, pipelines, and fuel depots.

Ukraine Equips S-5 Unguided Rockets on FPV Drones in Escalating Mid-Strike Campaign — Ukraine on Wednesday confirmed it had equipped some long-range drones with rocket launchers firing Soviet-era S-5 unguided rockets. The news comes amid Ukraine’s intensifying mid-range strikes targeting Russian logistics, though the idea of drone-launched missiles or rockets is not new.

Ukraine's MHP Plans to Buy 70% of Greek Poultry Producer Nitsiakos — The Ukrainian agrifood group intends to buy into Th. Nitsiakos AVEE, a vertically integrated Greek producer founded in the 1970s, reserving the right to full ownership in the future. Closing still hinges on regulatory clearances.

Romanian Leader Dan Calls on Kremlin to Hit Targets in Ukraine More Accurately — Romanian President Nicușor Dan expressed hope that Russia would strike Ukraine more precisely to avoid drones entering Romania, after a Russian Shahed hit a Galați apartment building on May 29, 2026, injuring two. He confirmed Russian responsibility but avoided criticizing Russia’s campaign. The remarks drew sharp criticism from Ukraine, while Zelensky praised Romania’s response.

Ukraine Syncs With 20th EU Sanctions Package, Targets Oil Firms, Drone Makers in Russia, Propaganda in Donbas — Ukraine has synchronized its sanctions policy with the EU’s 20th package, expanding pressure on Russia’s oil sector, drone manufacturers, and military-industrial supply chains. The updated list includes major firms such as Slavneft, UAV producers, and Rostec-linked officials, as well as entities involved in deportation and ideological indoctrination programs in occupied territories.

Ukraine Moves Toward Serial Production of Domestically Made Guided Aerial Bombs — BlueBird Tech says it is preparing serial production of Ukrainian-made guided aerial bombs in partnership with a design bureau and top engineers. The system, developed under the Brave1 cluster, features a 250-kg warhead and long-range precision strike capability. Ukraine’s defense ministry has already procured an initial test batch.

Trump Seeks Ukraine War Freeze Before Nov. 3 US Mid-Terms — Ukrainian officials believe “the US” may attempt to de-escalate or “calm down” the war in Ukraine ahead of the Nov. 3 mid-term elections, RBC-Ukraine reports citing sources in the government. Kyiv expects increased White House political involvement, including discussions on a possible freeze along current front lines with security guarantees. Officials stress that negotiations with Trump officials continue, though outcomes depend on bat

Pashinyan Rejects Referendum on Armenia’s EU vs Eurasian Union Future — Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan on Monday rejected calls for holding a referendum on whether Armenia should choose between the EU and the Eurasian Economic Union, saying the issue remains theoretical for now. He argued such a vote would only make sense once European integration reaches a more concrete stage.

Russia Imposes Jet Fuel Export Ban Amid Fuel Crisis — Russia imposed a jet fuel ban from June 1 to Nov. 30, following earlier restrictions on gasoline exports. The decision comes amid gasoline rationings in occupied areas as Ukrainian strikes continue to hit Russian oil infrastructure.

Ukraine Uses Decoy Drone Swarms, AI to Challenge Russian Air Defenses — Ukraine is increasingly using AI-assisted systems, decoy drone swarms and decentralized command networks for long-range strikes inside Russia, CNN reported on Thursday. A HUR commander said the system can coordinate thousands of UAVs simultaneously.

Kyiv Sees Opening for Talks Ahead of Winter as Russian Offensive Slows, Zelensky Says — Zelensky told CBS News that Russia has been losing battlefield initiative since late 2025, creating a potential “window for negotiations” before winter. He urged increased sanctions pressure on Moscow, said diplomatic talks depend on Russian readiness, and suggested possible mediators including the UK, France, Germany, Türkiye, and Nordic countries.

France, Partners Intercept Russian Oil Tanker — France said it detained the suspected Russian oil tanker Tagor in the Atlantic with UK and partners, targeting Moscow’s sanctions-evading “shadow fleet”. The vessel, flying a false Cameroonian flag and sailing from Murmansk toward Africa, was boarded by commandos for checks over irregular registration and sanctions breaches.

Romania Strike Exposes NATO’s Eastern Flank Risks — A Russian drone penetrated Romanian airspace and struck an apartment in Galați. The attack has caused significant implications. It is the most serious security breach of Romanian territory since the start of the Russian invasion in Ukraine, and it is a clear sign that the war is becoming a regional conflict.

Poland and Ukraine are Fighting the Past, and Only Moscow Gains — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s decision to grant an elite military unit the honorary title “Heroes of the UPA” has sparked a diplomatic dispute with Poland. While Ukraine views the UPA as independence fighters, Poland associates it with wartime massacres of Polish civilians. The controversy highlights enduring historical tensions and reflects broader shifts in Ukrainian wartime nationalism and Polish-Ukrainian relations

EU Weighs Limiting Protection for Ukrainian Men of Military Age in Potential Sixth-Year Extension — EU capitals are debating a possible extension of the Temporary Protection Directive for Ukrainians, while considering limits on eligibility for men of conscription age. The program, hosting over 4.3 million people, may be prolonged into a sixth year as officials discuss a gradual phase-out and long-term residency transition.

Book Arsenal 2026: Freedom, Responsibility and Culture in Wartime Ukraine — Kyiv’s Book Arsenal 2026 brought together leading Ukrainian and international writers, intellectuals, soldiers, and human rights advocates for four days of discussions on freedom, responsibility, memory, and culture during wartime. Speakers – including Maksym Butkevych, Oleksandra Matviichuk, Pavlo Kazarin, and Oksana Zabuzhko – reflected on Ukraine’s struggle for survival, the role of civic responsibility, and how cultu

Romania Identifies Drone Behind Strike on Apartment Block as Russian — Romania says technical analysis confirmed the drone that struck an apartment block in Galati was a Russian-origin Geran-2 used by Moscow’s forces, making Russia “solely responsible.” The incident injured two people and marked the first known drone hit on a residential building outside Ukraine since Russia’s full-scale invasion. Zelensky welcomed Romania’s findings and urged closer cooperation against shared threats.

US Strikes Iranian Drone Sites and Air Defenses Amid Fragile Ceasefire — The US military struck Iranian radar systems and drone command facilities, saying the operation responded to Iranian aggression including the downing of a US drone. Iran claimed retaliation against an American base and warned of stronger responses if attacks continue, while ceasefire conditions remain under strain.
